correctness.rationale: For the stated simple graph on Z_4^2, translations, coordinate interchange and (x,y)->(x,x−y) preserve D. Their nonzero offset orbits are D, the three order-two offsets Q, and C; C is not the full nonedge set. A singleton stops with 7 marked. Representatives of the three pair orbits have initial/final marked counts 10/10, 12/12 and 12/16 respectively; for (0,0),(1,2) the four listed forces have distinct unique unmarked targets. Thus all and only the 16·6/2=48 pairs of C are optimal. A jump keeps one endpoint, giving the line graph of the C-Cayley graph, and the displayed determinant-one linear map carries C onto D. For slides, the permissible partners of each fixed sensor induce two disjoint triangles under original adjacency. Splitting each fixed sensor into these two triangles gives the cubic graph H with one edge per optimal pair. Two edges meet precisely when the configurations keep a sensor and the two other endpoints are adjacent in G. The frozen 32-entry permutation was checked as data against the full edge sets and maps H onto the Dyck LCF graph. An independent exhaustive power-closure and graph reconstruction confirms both isomorphisms and both unordered distance histograms with the stated eccentricities. The rook comparison follows from the unmarked block with both sides at least two for two sensors, and the single unmarked cell for a triple meeting distinct rows and columns; the common degree and pair parameters yield cospectrality.
residual_risks: The checks are exhaustive for the stated finite graphs only. The frozen documentation lists Python 3.9 as sufficient, but verify_power_domination.py uses int.bit_count(), introduced in 3.10; use Python 3.10 or newer when replaying the frozen scripts. This is a version-note issue, not a gap in the graph claim or in the separate replay.

value.rationale: The Shrikhande graph is a canonical small strongly regular graph rather than an arbitrary board size. Its two relocation models give different classical line graphs, showing exactly how much restricting feasible moves to original edges changes optimal relocation distances. The identification explains the census and gives a reusable structural model. The cospectral rook twin illustrates that the common (16,6,2,2) parameters do not determine power-domination number; its known numerical value is not the main contribution.
residual_risks: There is no extension to all strongly regular graphs or to paths through temporarily nonoptimal configurations.
